import nki
import nki.isa as nisa
import nki.language as nl

@nki.jit
def tensor_transpose2D_kernel_(x, shape2D):
    P, F = x.shape
    F1, F2 = shape2D
    assert F1 * F2 == F, f"shape2D {shape2D} does not match the free size {F}"

    # Allocate output tile in shared HBM
    out = nl.ndarray((P, F), dtype=x.dtype, buffer=nl.shared_hbm)

    # Allocate input tile in SBUF
    in_tile = nl.ndarray((P, F1, F2), dtype=x.dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf)

    # DMA copy input to SBUF
    nisa.dma_copy(dst=in_tile, src=x)

    # Reshape and transpose in SBUF
    # Use affine_range to loop over partitions
    for p in nl.affine_range(P):
        # Slice the current partition
        tile_p = in_tile[p, :, :]

        # Transpose the 2D matrix in the tile
        transposed = tile_p.transpose(1, 2)

        # Write back to the output tile
        out[p, :] = transposed.flatten()

    return out

    P, F = x.shape
    F1, F2 = shape2D
    assert F1 * F2 == F, f"shape2D {shape2D} does not match the free size {F}"
    
    # Allocate output buffer in shared HBM
    out = nl.ndarray((P, F), dtype=x.dtype, buffer=nl.shared_hbm)
    
    # Allocate a tile for the data
    tile = nl.ndarray((128, 128), dtype=x.dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf)
    
    # Copy data from HBM to SBUF tile
    nisa.dma_copy(dst=tile, src=x)
    
    # Reshape and transpose within the tile
    # First, reshape the tile to (F1, F2) and transpose to (F2, F1)
    # Then reshape back to (F)
    # We need to handle the tiling manually since we can't reshape directly in NKI
    
    # Define the tile indices
    row_idx = nl.arange(128)
    col_idx = nl.arange(128)
    
    # Compute the transposed indices
    transposed_row = col_idx
    transposed_col = row_idx
    
    # Copy data from tile to output
    for i in nl.affine_range(128):
        for j in nl.affine_range(128):
            out[i, j] = tile[transposed_row[j], transposed_col[i]]
    
    return out
